title: Sunrise relay — quick scrub and escalation journal (03 Mar 2028)
content:
TL;DR: 03/03 sunrise relay — observed intermittent 95p token latency spikes for hosted/chat routes (eu-west1). Triggered an automated rollback to v1.4-quant while primary v2.0-q rolled back due to increased tail latency after node eviction. Mitigated by rate-limiter toggle + burst-capacity scale-up; next shift: follow up on autoscaler cooldown and per-pool eviction metric.

Timeline (local times):
- 02:58 AM: Alert fired — "chat-generation-95p-latency" (threshold 600ms). Pager to SRE rotation (Aisha).
- 03:01 AM: Quick probe: spike correlated with high KV cache miss rate and elevated scheduler pod reschedules in eu-west1-pool-3.
- 03:08 AM: Investigated node OOM events; two GPU nodes experienced mem-pressure and were drained by k8s. Scheduler rebalanced pods; some model-serving pods landed on burst hosts with different kernel page-size leading to slower kernels for v2.0-q.
- 03:12 AM: Automatic fallback to v1.4-quant (slower but more stable) started; overall requests experienced increased tail latency while caches warmed.
- 03:18 AM: Applied temporary per-route rate-limit (chat: 60rps -> 45rps) and promoted reserved burst nodes (scale +2). Latency improved gradually.
- 03:35 AM: Rolling restart of affected deployment to reattach persistent KV caches (runbook step 3b). Post-restart tail latency returned close to baseline.
- 04:05 AM: Pager cleared. Monitoring shows residual cache-miss spikes during cold starts for a 45 minute window.

What I ran (play-by-play):
- kubectl describe pod <pod-id> -> confirmed OOMKilled on two nodes; note pod IDs in ticket.
- queried x-prometheus:rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m]) to verify miss spike.
- toggled feature flag: enable_per-route-rate-limits via admin-api.
- scaled control-plane: provisioned 2 reserved burst nodes via internal autoscaler UI.
- reopened runbook step and annotated discrepancy (see runbook note below).

Immediate mitigation notes (for next shift):
- Keep per-route rate-limit at 45rps for chat routes until autoscaler cooldown adjusted. (Don't lower further without consulting infra on capacity — causes throughput backlog)
- Monitor kv_cache_miss_total and pod_reschedule_count; set alert if miss rate stays >2x baseline for more than 20m.
- If node OOM pattern repeats, isolate workload and cordon problematic node types; escalate to infra lead (Jonas) with SIGURG.

Root-cause hypothesis (first pass):
- Node mem-pressure + k8s reschedule => pods landed on suboptimal host configuration (different CPU kernel page-size + non-tuned CUDA drivers) => model runtime selected fallback kernels that are slower for v2.0-q; combined with cold KV caches produced 95p latency spikes.
- Secondary factor: autoscaler cooldown too short, allowing churn during recovery and not stabilizing cache warmup.

Runbook deltas (I annotated runbook v0.9: infra/runbooks/model-fallback-recovery.md):
- Add step to check node kernel version and driver sanity before allowing model variant rollout (new check 2.1).
- Add instruction to optionally pin model-variant to node-label "fast-kernel=true" when promoting v2 variants.
- Clarify guidance on rate-limits and scaling interplay (new note in 3b: "prefer scale-up over lowering route qps if backlog < 2k").
- Raise suggestion: expose per-pool eviction_count metric (INF-3421 created).

Open action items (owners + due dates):
- INF-3421 (Aisha) - create per-pool eviction_count metric and Grafana panel. Due 2028-03-08.
- INF-3422 (Jonas) - audit image/driver compatibility across eu-west1 node types, document mismatches. Due 2028-03-06.
- INF-3423 (Priya) - extend autoscaler cooldown for model-serving pools from 2m -> 6m (proposal in PR: /repo/infra#812). Due 2028-03-07.
- INF-3424 (Marco) - run synthetic warmup job for v2.0-q on 2-3 host types weekly to detect kernel fallback regressions. Due 2028-03-10.

Escalations + Communication:
- Notified Product-Eng (thread: slack #prod-eng, link in linked_artifacts). No customer-facing incident required at this time — impact within SLO except short-lived 95p blips.
- Chatted with Solutions Eng (Priya) to flag customers on Dedicated who might see higher token-latency; PR outreach queued if customers report degradation.

Handoff checklist for incoming shift (please ACK in the doc):
- [ ] Acknowledge this doc and tag next on-call.
- [ ] Confirm rate-limit still at 45rps; if lowered, note why in comments.
- [ ] Watch kv_cache_miss_total and pod_reschedule_count dashboards for 60 min.
- [ ] Verify INF-3421 metric appears (if not, ping Aisha).
- [ ] Make sure autoscaler-cooldown proposal PR has reviewer (Jonas/infra).
- [ ] If recurring OOMs appear, cordon affected nodes and open an incident with follow-up labeling.

Notes to self / weird bits to investigate (non-blocking):
- Why did k8s choose to reschedule to older kernel hosts? Is node-selector logic influenced by taints or affinity that we recently changed? Check infra/affinity-change PR history.
- The fallback-to-v1.4-quant happened automatically; need to double-check model-metadata version compat table — ensure rollout gating checks for "kernel mismatch".
- Observed a small uptick in api-gateway 5xx logs during the 03:00 window — probably backlog-related, logs at /var/log/gateway/2028-03-03.gz (I extracted 15m slice, saved in ticket INF-3421).

Useful links:
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INF-3421
- Runbook (annotated): https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/model-fallback-recovery
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/812
- Slack thread: #sre-ops (thread ts:1680302400.000200)

Sign-off: Aisha Patel (on-call)

Follow-up expectations for next shift (explicit):
- Confirm metric INF-3421 is emitting and add a short note in this doc once verified.
- If autoscaler cooldown change merges, observe live for 48 hours and revert if instability occurs.
- Revisit runbook notes and convert to a small PR (I left inline comments in runbook doc). Thanks!

Quick log (concise): 03:00 alert -> 03:12 fallback -> 03:18 rate-limit + scale -> 03:35 restart -> 04:05 clear. Remaining: cache-warm window ~45m.
